jobs.title: AI Product Engineer (Fullstack)
jobs.description:
The Role
  
  
We're looking for an
  
  
AI Product Engineer
  
  
who wants to own real product problems end to end.
  
  
We don't separate product engineering from customer problems. Engineers stay close to users and face their real business problems rather than optimize technology in isolation. You might start by understanding a workflow, ingesting and structuring the customer's context, shaping the experience, building across the stack, improving an agent or integration, shipping it, and learning from real use.
  
  
You do not need to be an expert in everything. We are building a team of
  
  
T-shaped engineers
  
  
: broad enough to own a product experience end to end, with meaningful depth in at least one area such as frontend, backend, mobile, data, AI systems, infrastructure, or integrations.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  
Own product features end to end.
  
  
Go from discovery and solution design through implementation, testing, deployment, operation, and iteration.
  
  
Build production AI systems.
  
  
Create agents that use tools and customer context to complete real business workflows, learn through feedback loops and long-term memory, and become more useful over time, supported by practical evaluation and observability.
  
  
Connect AI to real business systems.
  
  
Build reliable integrations and data flows across advertising, social media platforms, CRM, analytics, payments, and other platforms.
  
  
Work directly with customers.
  
  
Understand their business, workflow, technology stack, and pain points instead of receiving every problem through layers of abstraction.
  
  
Turn recurring pain into product.
  
  
When onboarding, data ingestion, an integration, or an AI output is consistently slow, low-quality, or unreliable, find the underlying product, architecture, or agent problem and make the system better for the next hundred customers.
  
  
Who You Are
  
  
You have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience shipping and operating real production systems. More importantly:
  
  
You can take an ambiguous problem, investigate it deeply, create structure, and own it through to a working outcome.
  
  
You are comfortable crossing technical boundaries and learning whatever the problem requires.
  
  
You have meaningful depth in at least one technical area and enough breadth to collaborate across the rest of the product.
  
  
You care whether what you build creates a useful customer outcome, not only whether the implementation works.
  
  
You use AI throughout your engineering workflow to research, prototype, write, review, test, debug, and learn, while exercising judgment about the quality of its output.
  
  
You understand that production agent engineering is more than prompting and are interested in the systems around the model: tools, context, retrieval, evaluation, state, reliability, and user interaction.
  
  
You communicate openly and are comfortable collaborating with customers, product managers, designers, and other engineers.
  
  
Bonus Points
  
  
You do not need all of these. We are especially interested if you have depth in one or more of the following:
  
  
You have shipped an LLM- or agent-powered product used by real customers.
  
  
You have hands-on experience with agent evaluation, tool use, retrieval, long-running workflows, or agent infrastructure.
  
  
You have built large-scale data ingestion or synchronization systems.
  
  
You have integrated advertising, social media, CRM, analytics, payment, or other business platforms.
  
  
You have worked directly with customers in product engineering, forward-deployed engineering, solutions engineering, consulting, or an agency.
  
  
You understand marketing workflows, marketing technology, or how businesses acquire and engage customers.
  
  
Why Join Us
  
  
You will have genuine ownership of both the product and the technology behind it. You will work closely with users and leadership, see the impact of what you build, and have the freedom to challenge how things currently work.
  
  
You will not be adding a chatbot to the edge of an established product. You will be building products where agents, context, tools, data, integrations, and user experience are all part of the core architecture.
  
  
Our culture is different from a typical software company. We grew from content creation, so we combine engineering rigor with storytelling, speed, experimentation, and a desire to make things people care about. The team shares ownership and passion for the company's success. You grow quickly, build close friendships, and find meaning in creating something ambitious together.

jobs.description:
Company Overview
  
  
3echo is a Singapore-based AI company building agent-powered products for businesses across Southeast Asia. We deploy AI agents that do real work — content production, operations, client delivery — measured by business outcomes, not features shipped. Small team, founder-led, fast iteration, paying clients.
  
  
The Role
  
  
You're an AI Engineer who ships end to end. Not a prompt tinkerer, not a pure backend dev — you sit where the agent workflow, the generative media pipeline, and the client's actual business outcome meet. You'll work directly with the founder in a small, fast team where your code goes to paying clients in days, not quarters.
  
  
**Mid-level:** 2–4 years shipping real systems. What matters more than years is that you've built things people use and that Claude is how you work. We're a Claude-native shop: Claude Code is the primary development environment, MCP is the integration layer, and agent skills are how we encode process. One engineer here ships what a team of five ships elsewhere, because the leverage is the tooling. If you're not already working this way, you should be hungry to.
  
  
What You'll Own
  
  
1. Agent & Workspace infrastructure
  
  

* Build and maintain MCP servers, agent skills, and workflow orchestration that power client Workspaces
* Encode business rules — budget gates, approval SLAs, credit accounting, sign-off rituals as self-enforcing agent behavior
* Automation pipelines in n8n connecting our register, comms, and client channels

2. Generative media pipeline
  
  

* Operate and extend the Studio engine: image generation (gpt-image-2), video generation (Seedance 2.0 via BytePlus), reference-anchored character consistency, take/cut/release pipelines
* Cost-aware generation: quota management, credit metering, resolution strategy, provider failover
* QA tooling for identity hold, canon compliance, and output quality

3. Full-stack product & client delivery
  
  

* Backend services in Python/FastAPI and TypeScript, Postgres/Supabase, deployed on GCP Cloud Run
* Client-facing surfaces in React where the Workspace needs a UI
* Forward-deployed work: onboarding client Workspaces, debugging live jobs, turning client feedback into shipped fixes fast

Our stack
  
  
Claude & Claude Code · MCP · n8n · gpt-image-2 · Seedance 2.0 (BytePlus) · Gemini (OpenRouter) · Python/FastAPI · TypeScript/React · Postgres/Supabase · Docker · GCP Cloud Run · on-prem RTX 5090 GPU servers
  
  
You don't need to know all of it. You need to be dangerous in most of it within your first month.
  
  
You've probably done some of this
  
  

* Shipped an LLM-powered product or agent system to real users (side projects count if they're live)
* Built with tool-calling / MCP / function-calling APIs, not just chat completions
* Worked with generative image or video APIs and dealt with their failure modes
* Owned a backend service in production — deploys, logs, incidents, the unglamorous parts
* Ship daily with Claude Code (or equivalent) as your primary environment — you know how to scope tasks for an agent, review its output critically, and get 5–10× throughput from it, not 1.2×
* Written system prompts, skills, or MCP tools that made a model reliably do a job — you treat the model as a system to engineer, not a chatbot to talk to

How we hire
  
  
We hire on
  
  
AI DNA
  
  
: attitude, learning curve, hunger. Certifications and brand-name employers don't move us. A GitHub repo, a live demo, or a story about the hardest thing you shipped moves us a lot. Attitude disqualifies faster than ability qualifies.
  
  
Part of the interview is watching you work with Claude on a real task. We're not testing whether you can code without AI, we're testing how much more you can do with it.
  
  
First 90 days — what success looks like
  
  

* Week 2: shipped your first fix to a live client Workspace
* Month 1: own one of the three pillars day-to-day with the founder reviewing, not driving
* Month 3: a client outcome (turnaround, first-pass rate, or cost-per-deliverable) measurably improved by something you built

How to apply
  
  
**Email Benjamin@3echo.ai with:**  
1. A link to something you built (repo, demo, live product)
  
  
2. Three sentences on the hardest technical problem you've solved
  
  
Interested candidates are encouraged to apply via this platform. We look forward to your applications!
  
  
3echo is a Singapore-based AI company building agent-powered products for businesses across Southeast Asia. Summary of Position
  
  
The Critical and Emerging Technologies Division's Singapore office is ASTM's Asia hub, working with regional research institutes,industry, and standards bodies to move critical and emerging technology standards from research question to adopted practice. Regional demand has shifted beyond additive manufacturing to AI and robotics, in support of ASTM Committees F45 (Robotics, Automation, and Autonomous Systems), F48 (Exoskeletons andExosuits), and F50 (Artificial Intelligence in Manufacturing Systems). F50 alone drew more than 100 organizations from over 20 countries within months of its formation in 2026. Meeting that demand takes hands-on robotics and AIengineering capability on the Singapore team. This is a newly created technical position established to build it.
  
  
We are seeking a technically grounded, self-directed, and collaborative AI and Robotics Engineer within ASTM who will bring demonstrated robotics and AI engineering expertise to the division's standards, qualification, and program work in Asia. In general, the Engineer will be the technical focal point in the region for AI and robotics standards activity: identifying standards gaps, supporting work items and pre-standardization research, designing and running the test and evaluation work behind them, and connecting regional technical partners to ASTM's committees and programs, which includes training and certification programs
  
  
The division develops standards alongside thetechnology rather than years later, which puts a premium on getting the technical work right the first time. This role owns its technical judgments, documents them, and stands behind them.
  
  
**Specifically, the AI and Robotics Engineer, will:**  

* Support standards development in Committees F45, F48, and F50: draft and review technical content for work items, contribute to task groups, coordinate research-to-standards projects, and track ballots and committee actions relevant to the region.
* Conduct gap analyses and roadmapping for AI and robotics standards, working with the division's robotics lead and Data and AI group, so that regional work aligns with division roadmaps.
* Planand deliver applied research, pilot projects, and test and evaluation on AI and robotic systems with regional partners, from technical scoping through test method development, instrumentation, data collection, analysis, and final report.
* Develop and deliver training and support certification and qualification programs in AI and robotics, including course content, instruction, and assessment and credential development aligned to the relevant standards.
* Provide technical content and program support for the division's AI and robotics convenings run from Singapore, including the AI and robotics tracks of ICAM, standalone robotics or AI events, Snapshot Workshops, and partner-hosted technical sessions, working with the Events team.
* Engage regional research institutes, national program offices, industry, and standards bodies (for example A\*STAR, ARTC, the National Robotics Programme, and Enterprise Singapore) on technical matters, and bring their experts into ASTM committee work.
* Track developments in AI and robotics standardization, regulation, and industry practice across Asia, and translate them into technical briefings, reports, and presentations for internal leadership, committee audiences, and regional partners.
* Take initiative on work outside the immediate assignment when it serves the program, and keep the Regional Director, Asia informed without needing to be asked.

Please note that some travel will be required for this position (approximately 15-20%).
  
  
Minimum Qualifications
  
  

* Bachelor's degree in robotics, mechatronics, computer science, electrical or mechanical engineering, artificial intelligence, or a closely related technical field.
* Minimum of 3 years of hands-on industry or applied research experience in robotics, autonomous systems, or applied AI and machine learning. Experience in manufacturing or materials engineering alone does not meet this requirement.
* Demonstrated hands-on engineering work: programming, integrating, or commissioning roboticor autonomous systems, or developing, training, and validating AI and machine learning models in a production or laboratory setting.
* Working proficiency in Python, and with robotics middleware such as ROS or ROS 2, or with mainstream machine learning frameworks.
* Demonstrated experience designing and running test and evaluation of robotic or AI system performance, safety, or reliability, with documented methods and results.
* Demonstrated ability to run technical projects end to end: scoping, execution, documentation, and reporting.
* Working knowledge of how technical standards are developed and used, or the ability tolearn ASTM's consensus process quickly.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including technical writing for committee and partner audiences.
* Highly dependable, reliable, responsible, responsive, resourceful, and independent individual who is flexible and adaptive.
* Ability to work closely with a diverse group of staff, technical committees, individual technical experts, and contractors.
* Abilityto maintain confidentiality of sensitive organizational information.
* Eligibilityto work in Singapore.

Preferred Qualifications
  
  

* Master's degree or PhD in robotics, artificial intelligence, or a closely related technical field.
* Experience applying robotics or AI safety, performance, or testing standards and frameworks, including international references (for example ISO 10218, ISO13482, ISO/IEC 42001, or the NIST AI Risk Management Framework).
* Familiarity with standardization bodies such as ASTM, ISO, IEC, or other regulatory organizations, and with the standards ecosystems of Singapore and the wider region.
* Experience organizing or contributing technical content to conferences, workshops, or industry events.
* Experience working with research institutes, consortia, or public agencies in Asia.
* Established professional network across Asia's robotics, AI, research, and standards communities.
* Passion for innovation, technology, and enterprise development.

About the CET Division
  
  
ASTM International's Critical and EmergingTechnologies (CET) Division convenes industry, government, and academia, accelerating the path to standards for the technologies reshaping the global economy. The division engages these technologies at the intersections where standards are needed most, which creates the opportunity to develop standards alongside technologies rather than years after they have spread across society.Its work runs in three stages: pre-standardization gap identification, consensus-based standardization, and post-standardization adoption support. Its technical committees cover additive and advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence in manufacturing systems, autonomous systems and robotics, commercial spaceflight, and unmanned aircraft systems, delivered through the ASTM AM Center of Excellence, the ASCET Center of Excellence, Wohlers Associates, and the ICAM conference. Roughly 60 staff operate across 12 timezones and four continents. The division moves at the pace of the industries it serves, and it holds the work to the evidence.
  
  
About ASTM International
  
  
ASTM International is an international standards organization that develops and publishes voluntary consensus technical standards for a wide range of materials, products, systems, and services. Over 13,000 ASTM standards operate globally. Defined and set by ASTM, these standards improve the lives of millions every day. Combined with our innovative business services, they enhance performance and help people around the world have confidence in the things they buy and use. The organization's headquartersis in West Conshohocken, Pennsylvania, about 5 mi (8.0 km) northwest of Philadelphia. Founded in 1898 as the American Section of the International Association for Testing Materials, ASTM International predates other standardsorganizations such as the BSI (1901), IEC (1906), DIN (1917), ANSI (1918), AFNOR (1926), and ISO (1947).
  
  
Over 12,800 ASTM Standards operate globally. Defined and set by us, they improve the lives of millions every day. Combined with our innovative business services, they enhance performance and help everyone have confidence in the things they buy and use.

jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer - Agentic AI Evaluation
jobs.description:
About Us
  
  
Resaro is an independent, third-party AI assurance company. We build the software and run the evaluations that let enterprises and public-sector bodies deploy AI they can actually trust - across computer vision, LLMs, vision-language models, and, increasingly, agentic and autonomous systems, for clients in government, defence, and regulated commercial sectors.
  
  
Our product, the Approved Intelligence Platform (AIP), is where this becomes real software: customers register the AI systems they want tested, run rigorous evaluations, and produce defensible, auditable evidence and reports. Agentic AI is moving from pilots into operational, high-stakes deployments faster than anyone can assure it - the overwhelming majority of agent pilots still fail before production, on governance, traceability, and reliability gaps rather than raw capability. Closing that gap is the product. That's what you'll build.
  
  
The Role
  
  
We're hiring a senior engineer to be our go-to person for agentic AI evaluation - the technical owner of how AIP measures whether tool-using, multi-step agents are fit to deploy. You'll build the evaluation engine behind our agentic MVP and the roadmap beyond it, and you'll be the person the team turns to when an agentic question is hard. As autonomous and embodied systems mature, you'll help extend the same rigour into those emerging areas.
  
  
This is a hands-on individual-contributor role with domain ownership. You report to the Engineering Manager for the evaluation engine and partner closely with Product, who owns the roadmap. You set the technical bar for this vertical; you don't line-manage.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  
Own the agentic-evaluation engine. Build the capability that scores agents on the metrics that matter - intent resolution, tool-selection and parameterisation accuracy, task adherence, planning quality, tool-call ordering, response completeness against a reference, and when an agent should defer to a human.
  
  
Evaluate stateful, multi-turn behaviour - not single prompts. Agents carry memory and act over long horizons; your harnesses must expose how behaviour drifts, degrades, or becomes unsafe across a session.
  
  
**Make evaluation trustworthy. Design for evaluator integrity:** isolate the runner from the agent, assert on semantics not just structure, count crashed/incomplete tasks as failures, audit ground truth, and build tests that probe the test setup itself. A benchmark you can't trust is worse than none.
  
  
Build the agentic-security surface. Partner on red-teaming and adversarial evaluation - tool-chain exploits, RBAC and permission-inheritance failures, multi-turn safety erosion - so we catch what a motivated adversary would.
  
  
Close the lab-to-production gap. Design evaluations that surface where agents that look good in a demo fail in a real, customer-specific deployment - the gap that makes independent assurance necessary.
  
  
Translate governance into engineering. Work with our governance analysts to turn EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO 42001 requirements into concrete, testable evaluation logic.
  
  
Set the technical bar for the vertical - through spikes, ADRs, and code review - and keep your reasoning legible so the team can build on it.
  
  
Extend into emerging autonomy. As embodied and other autonomous systems become real evaluation targets, help us adapt the engine to them.
  
  
What We're Looking For
  
  
5+ years of professional software engineering, shipping and operating production systems (not prototypes) in Python.
  
  
Demonstrated depth in agentic AI - you've built, orchestrated, or rigorously evaluated LLM agents, and understand tool-calling, memory, multi-step control flow, and modern interoperability (MCP for tools, A2A for agent-to-agent) at more than a tutorial level.
  
  
A real grasp of how agents are measured - and how measurement fails. You know the standard execution-based benchmarks (GAIA, τ²-bench, OSWorld, SWE-bench Verified, WebArena) and why a high benchmark score routinely overstates production reliability.
  
  
Strong engineering judgement - you can take an ambiguous, research-adjacent problem, scope it, decompose it, and drive it to a shipped, tested, observable outcome without close supervision.
  
  
A genuine bias to go deep and stay hands-on, paired with the communication to be the person others come to for this domain - you document decisions and leave work others can pick up.
  
  
Clear written and verbal communication, and comfort being measured against concrete quarterly outcomes, including across a distributed Singapore-Europe team.
  
  
Nice To Have
  
  
Agentic security / red-teaming experience - adversarial testing, jailbreak/tool-chain exploits, or agent identity and on-behalf-of authorisation.
  
  
Evaluation, testing, or assurance tooling for any AI domain — LLM/RAG, agentic, or computer vision - including LLM-as-judge pipelines and their failure modes.
  
  
Familiarity with AI governance frameworks (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001) and translating principles into engineering requirements.
  
  
Emerging embodied / autonomous AI exposure - vision-language-action models, simulators, or world-model approaches (a plus, not a requirement).
  
  
Data-intensive pipelines with columnar/lakehouse formats (Parquet/Iceberg) and DuckDB or similar.
  
  
Container-based or serverless execution frameworks (Nuclio or comparable) for running evaluations at scale.
  
  
Kubernetes/Helm and GPU/CUDA infrastructure for model inference.
  
  
Experience where evidence, auditability, and reproducibility were first-class requirements (regulated, safety-critical, or defence contexts).
  
  
Our Hiring Blueprint
  
  
We hire to a high, transparent bar. We look for production-grade code (correct, tested, observable, maintainable by others); communication and handover (you write clearly and document decisions); independent operation (you scope and drive ambiguous problems to shipped outcomes); and a T-shaped profile - deep in agentic AI evaluation, broad enough to operate across the stack and the ML-evaluation domain.
  
  
Resaro is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We respect each individual and support the diverse cultures, perspectives, skills and experiences within our teams.
